summary_zh.motivation: 控制选区激光熔化残余应力
summary_zh.method: 提出3D激光冲击喷丸方法调控残余应力
summary_zh.result: 成功实现残余应力的三维控制

summary_en.motivation: To develop a method for three-dimensional control of residual stresses in selective laser melted parts.
summary_en.method: A 3D laser shock peening technique is proposed and applied to SLM-fabricated samples to modify residual stress distribution.
summary_en.result: The method effectively controls residual stresses in three dimensions, reducing tensile stresses and inducing compressive stresses.
summary_en.validation: Residual stresses were measured experimentally using X-ray diffraction before and after peening, confirming the stress redistribution.

papers.title: Numerical and experimental evaluation of a conformally cooled H13 steel injection mould manufactured with selective laser melting
papers.first_author_affiliation: RMIT Centre for Additive Manufacturing, School Engineering, RMIT University, Melbourne, Australia

corresponding_authors.name: Maciej Mazur
corresponding_authors.affiliation: RMIT Centre for Additive Manufacturing, School Engineering, RMIT University, Melbourne, Australia

llm.relevance_to_user: 论文讨论的是H13工具钢注塑模具的随形冷却，与生物医学植入物的应力屏蔽、多孔结构、疲劳测试等完全无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on conformal cooling in injection moulds made of H13 tool steel, not on biomedical implants, porous structures, stress shielding, fatigue testing, or osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 优化注塑模具冷却效率与均匀性。
summary_zh.method: 采用SLM制造随形冷却H13钢模具，结合数值模拟分析热行为。
summary_zh.result: 随形冷却显著提升了冷却均匀性并缩短了循环时间。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验测量模具温度分布验证数值模拟结果。

summary_en.motivation: To improve cooling efficiency and uniformity in injection moulding by optimizing cooling channel design.
summary_en.method: Selective laser melting was used to fabricate H13 steel moulds with conformal cooling channels, and numerical simulations were performed to predict thermal behavior.
summary_en.result: Conformal cooling channels significantly improved cooling uniformity and reduced cycle time compared to conventional channels.
summary_en.validation: Numerical predictions were validated against experimental temperature measurements on the fabricated mould.

papers.title: Structure, Texture and Phases in 3D Printed IN718 Alloy Subjected to Homogenization and HIP Treatments
papers.abstract: 3D printing results in anisotropy in the microstructure and mechanical properties. The focus of this study is to investigate the structure, texture and phase evolution of the as-printed and heat treated IN718 superalloy. Cylindrical specimens, printed by powder-bed additive manufacturing technique, were subjected to two post-treatments: homogenization (1100 °C, 1 h, furnace cooling) and hot isostatic pressing (HIP) (1160 °C, 100 MPa, 4 h, furnace cooling). The Selective laser melting (SLM) printed microstructure exhibited a columnar architecture, parallel to the building direction, due to the heat flow towards negative z-direction. Whereas, a unique structural morphology was observed in the x-y plane due to different cooling rates resulting from laser beam overlapping. Post-processing treatments reorganized the columnar structure of a strong {002} texture into fine columnar and/or equiaxed grains of random orientations. Equiaxed structure of about 150 µm average grain size, was achieved after homogenization and HIP treatments. Both δ-phase and MC-type brittle carbides, having rough morphologies, were formed at the grain boundaries. Delta-phase formed due to γ″-phase dissolution in the γ matrix, while MC-type carbides nucleates grew by diffusion of solute atoms. The presence of (Nb0.78Ti0.22)C carbide phase, with an fcc structure having a lattice parameter a = 4.43 Å, was revealed using Energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) and X-ray diffractometer (XRD) analysis. The solidification behavior of IN718 alloy was described to elucidate the evolution of different phases during selective laser melting and post-processing heat treatments of IN718.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the anisotropy in microstructure and mechanical properties of 3D printed IN718 superalloy.
summary_en.method: Cylindrical specimens were fabricated by selective laser melting and subjected to homogenization and hot isostatic pressing, followed by microstructural analysis using XRD and EDS.
summary_en.result: Post-treatments transformed the columnar {002} texture into fine columnar or equiaxed grains with random orientations, and promoted formation of δ-phase and MC-type carbides at grain boundaries.
summary_en.validation: Phase identification and crystallographic analysis were performed using energy dispersive spectrometry and X-ray diffractometry.
